For adults with asthma, **as-needed low-dose inhaled corticosteroid (ICS)-formoterol** is preferred as a reliever therapy over short-acting beta-agonist (SABA) alone, even at the mildest asthma step, to reduce exacerbation risk [GINA, 2024]. 

This recommendation is based on evidence that combination therapy provides better control of airway inflammation and reduces the risk of acute exacerbations compared to SABA monotherapy. 

**Disclaimer:** This guidance is intended for professional review and should not be used for diagnosis or treatment planning without clinical evaluation. 

**Citation:** Global Strategy for Asthma Management, GINA, 2024. https://ginasthma.org/2026-gina-strategy-report/
